hardness_rationale: The seed asks for two-digit numbers divisible by each of their digits; this reduces to manageable casework and simple divisibility checks. Our family strengthens and entangles constraints in three ways: (1) numbers can have 3 or 4 digits, vastly expanding the search space; (2) each valid number must be divisible not only by each nonzero digit but also by the sum of its digits, which introduces a global digit-sum modulus that interacts nontrivially with per-digit divisibility; and (3) we require the gcd of the nonzero digits to equal a specified value and enforce a minimum number of distinct nonzero digits, which prevents easy single-digit/gcd trivialities and forces careful structural reasoning (e.g., parity constraints, presence of 5 implying trailing zeros, compatibility of digit-sum divisibility with lcm of digits). Solving analytically now demands combining lcm/gcd insights, modular arithmetic with digit sums, and exclusion of many impossible digit patterns, making it considerably more difficult than the seed.
notes:
Proof outline and correctness justification: For any N, “N divisible by each nonzero digit” is equivalent to N being divisible by L = lcm of its nonzero digits. The added constraint “N divisible by the sum of its digits s” further implies N is a multiple of M = lcm(L, s). Thus a necessary condition is N ∈ {multiples of M in the d-digit interval}. The gcd constraint g = gcd(nonzero digits) = g_target ensures every nonzero digit is a multiple of g_target, and in particular L is a multiple of g_target; this is a strong structural filter on allowed digit sets. The minimum distinct nonzero digits condition prevents degenerate cases with a single nonzero digit determining the gcd for free.
To prove the algorithm computes the correct sum: the verifier enumerates all d-digit N and applies tests that are exactly the four constraints stated in the problem. These tests are both necessary and sufficient by definition of S; hence the set collected equals S, and summing it returns the desired quantity. For manual contest-style reasoning, one can systematically restrict digits using: (i) if a digit 5 appears, then N must be a multiple of 5, which combined with divisibility by even digits may force N to be a multiple of 10; (ii) requiring N ≡ 0 mod s bounds N to multiples of s within the interval and interacts with divisibility by 3 and 9 via s; (iii) gcd constraints imply all digits lie in an arithmetic progression of allowed residues (multiples of g_target), severely limiting candidate digit sets. From these, one performs casework on digit compositions and uses lcm constraints to test compatibility, ultimately enumerating S and summing. The verifier enforces nontriviality (at least 3 solutions and not too many), ensuring instances are challenging enough for training while remaining tractable.
source_question: Find the sum of all positive two-digit integers that are divisible by each of their digits.
